verses.sanskrit: गान्धार्युवाच।अध्यर्धगुणमाहुर्यं बले शौर्ये च केशव। पित्रा त्वया च दाशार्ह दृप्तं सिंहमिवोत्कटम्॥१॥
यो बिभेद चमूमेको मम पुत्रस्य दुर्भिदाम्। स भूत्वा मृत्युरन्येषां स्वयं मृत्युवशं गतः॥२॥
तस्योपलक्षये कृष्ण कार्ष्णेरमिततेजसः। अभिमन्योर्हतस्यापि प्रभा नैवोपशाम्यति॥३॥
एषा विराटदुहिता स्नुषा गाण्डीवधन्वनः। आर्ता बालं पतिं वीरं दृष्ट्वा शोचत्यनिन्दिता॥४॥
verses.english: There, the daughter of Virata, the daughterin-law of Arjuna, that girl of faultless beauty, stricken with grief on seeing her heroic husband, is bewailing.

verses.sanskrit: तमेषा हि समागम्य भार्या भर्तारमन्तिके। विराटदुहिता कृष्ण पाणिना परिमार्जति॥५॥
verses.english: Approaching her husband, that young wife, viz., the daughter of Virata, is gently rubbing him, O Krishna, with her hand.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य वक्त्रमुपाघ्राय सौभद्रस्य मनस्विनी। विबुद्धकमलाकारं कम्बुवृत्तशिरोधरम्॥६॥
verses.english: Formerly, that highly intelligent and beautiful girl, inebriate with honied wines, used bashfully to embrace her lord, and kiss and face of Subhadra's son, resembling a fullblown lotus and supported on a neck bearing three lines like those of a conch-shell.

verses.sanskrit: कामरूपवती चैषा परिष्वजति भामिनी। लज्जमाना पुरा चैनं माध्वीकमदमूर्च्छिता॥७॥
तस्य क्षतजसन्दिग्धं जातरूपपरिष्कृतम्। विमुच्य कवचं कृष्ण शीरमभिवीक्षते॥८॥
अवेक्षमाणा तं बाला कुष्ण त्वामभिभाषते। अयं ते पुण्डरीकाक्ष सदृशाक्षो निपातितः॥९॥
verses.english: Beholding her lord, O Krishna, that girl addresses you saying:-'O lotus-eyed one, this hero whose eyes resembled yours, has been killed.

verses.sanskrit: बले वीर्ये च सदृशस्तेजसा चैव तेऽनघ। रूपेण च तथाऽत्यर्थं शेते भुवि निपातितः॥१०॥
अत्यन्तं सुकुमारस्य राङ्कवाजिनशायिनः। कच्चिदद्य शरीरं ते भूमौ न परितप्यते॥११॥
मातङ्गभुजवर्ष्णाणौ ज्याक्षेपकठिनत्वचौ। काञ्चनाङ्गदिनौ शेते निक्षिप्य विपुलौ भुजौ॥१२॥
verses.english: Stretching your massive arms decorated with golden Angadas, resembling a couple of elephants trunks, and trunks, and coated with skin hardened by constant use of the bow, sleep, you, O lord, peacefully as if worn out with the fatigue of too much exercise. Alas, why do you not speak to me that am weeping so?

verses.sanskrit: व्यायम्य बहुधा नूनं सुखसुप्तः श्रमादिव। एवं विलपतीमार्तां न हि मामभिभाषसे॥१३॥
न स्मराम्यपराधं ते किं मां न प्रतिभाषसे। ननु मां त्वं पुरा दूरादभिवीक्ष्याभिभाषसे॥१४॥
verses.english: I do not remember to have ever offered you. Why do you not speak to me then? Formerly, you used to addressed me even when you would see me at a distance.

verses.sanskrit: न स्मराम्यपराधं मे किं मां न प्रतिभाषसे। आर्यामार्य सुभद्रां त्वमिमांश्च त्रिदशोपमान्॥१५॥
पितॄन्मां चैव दुःखार्तां विहाय क्व गमिष्यसि। तस्य शोणितदिग्धान्वै केशानुद्यम्य पाणिना॥१६॥
verses.english: Where will you go, leaving behind you the much-respected Subhadra, these your sires who take after the very celestials, and my own wretched self distracted with grief.

verses.sanskrit: उत्सङ्गे वक्त्रमाधाय जीवन्तमिव पृच्छति। स्वस्रीयं वासुदेवस्य पुत्रं गाण्डीवधन्वनः॥१७॥
verses.english: See, O Krishna, collecting with her hands the blood-dyed hair of her husband and placing his head on her lap, beautiful lady is addressing him as if he were alive,-How could those great car-warriors kill you in the midst of battle,-you who are the sister's son of Vasudeva and the son of the bolder of Gandiva?

verses.sanskrit: कथं त्वां रणमध्यस्थं जघ्नुरेते महारथाः। धिगस्तु क्रूरकर्तॄंस्तान्कृपकर्णजयद्रथान्॥१८॥
द्रोणद्रौणायनी चोभौ यैरहं विधवा कृता। रथर्षभाणां सर्वेषां कथमासीत्तदा मनः॥१९॥
verses.english: Alas, fie on those wicked warriors, Kripa, Karna, Jayadratha, Drona and Drona's son, by whom you were killed!

verses.sanskrit: बालं त्वां पिरवार्यैकं मम दुःखाय जघ्नुषाम्। कथं नु पाण्डवानां च पाञ्चालानां तु पश्यताम्॥२०॥
त्वं वीर निधनं प्राप्तो नाथवान्सन्ननाथवत्। दृष्ट्वा बहुभिराक्रन्दे निहतं त्वां पिता तव॥२१॥
verses.english: How could you, O hero, who had so many protectors, be killed so helplessly before the very eyes of the Pandavas and the Panchalas?

verses.sanskrit: वीरः पुरुषशार्दूलः कथं जीवति पाण्डवः। न राज्यलाभो विपुलः शत्रूणां च पराभवः॥२२॥
verses.english: Seeing you, O hero, killed in battle by many warriors in a body, how is that foremost of men, that son of Pandu, viz., your father, able to bear the burden of life?

verses.sanskrit: प्रीतिं धास्यति पार्थानां त्वामृते पुष्करेक्षण। तव शस्त्रजिताँल्लोकान्धर्मेण च दमेन च॥२३॥
verses.english: Neither the acquisition of a vast territory, nor the discomfitures of their foes, gives joy to the Parthas bereft of you, O lotus-eyed one.

verses.sanskrit: क्षिप्रमन्वागमिष्यामि तत्र मां प्रतिपालय। दुर्मरं पुनरप्राप्ते काले भवति केनचित्॥२४॥
verses.english: By the practice of virtue and self-restraint, I shall very soon go to those blissful regions which you have acquired by the use of weapons. Protect me, O hero, when I go there.

verses.sanskrit: यदहं त्वां रणे दृष्ट्वा हतं जीवामि दुर्भगा। कामिदानीं नरव्याघ्र श्लक्ष्णया स्मितया गिरा॥२५॥
verses.english: Until the appointed time comes, one cannot die, since, wretched that I am, I am still alive after seeing you killed in battle.

verses.sanskrit: पितृलोके समेत्यान्यां मामिवामन्त्रयिष्यसि। नूनमप्सरसां स्वर्गे मनांसि प्रमथिष्यसि॥२६॥
verses.english: Having gone to the region of the departed manes, whom else, like me, do you address now, O foremost of men, in sweet and smiling words.

verses.sanskrit: परमेण च रूपेण गिरा च स्मितपूर्वया। प्राप्य पुण्यकृताँल्लोकानप्सरोभिः समेयिवान्॥२७॥
verses.english: Forsooth, you will agitated the hearts of the Apsaras in heaven, with your great beauty and soft and smiling words.

verses.sanskrit: सौभद्र विहरन् काले स्मरेथाः सुकृतानि मे। एतावानिह संवासो विहितस्ते मया सह॥२८॥
verses.english: Having attained the regions reserved for pious persons, you are now united, O son of Subhadra, with the Apsaras. While playing with them, recollect now and then my good acts towards you.

verses.sanskrit: षण्मासान्सप्तमे मासि त्वं वीर निधनं गतः। इत्युक्तवचनामेनामपकर्षन्ति दुःखिताम्॥२९॥
उत्तरां मोघसङ्कल्पां मत्स्यराजकुलस्त्रियः। उत्तरामपकृष्यैनामार्तामार्ततराः स्वयम्॥३०॥
verses.english: O Krishna, the ladies of the royal house of Matsya are dragging away the sorrowful Uttara, disappointed, and even lamenting in this way.

verses.sanskrit: विराटं निहतं दृष्ट्वा क्रोशन्ति विलपन्ति च। द्रोणास्त्रशरसङ्कृत्तं शयानं रुधिरोक्षितम्॥३१॥
verses.english: Dragging away the sorrow-stricken Uttara, those ladies, themselves still more aggrieved then that girl, are weeping and bewailing aloud at sight of the slain Virata.

verses.sanskrit: विराटं वितुदन्त्येते गृध्रगोमायुवायसाः। वितुद्यमानं विहगैर्विराटमसितेक्षणाः॥३२॥
verses.english: Wounded with the weapons and arrows of Drona, lying down oi. earth, and bathed in blood, Virata is encompassed by the screaming vultures and yelling jackals and crows ravens.

verses.sanskrit: न शक्नुवन्ति विहगान्निवारयितुमातुराः। आसामातपतप्तानामायासेन च योषिताम्॥३३॥
verses.english: Those black-eyed ladies, approaching the dead body of Matsya king over which carnivorous birds are uttering cries of joy, are trying to turn the body. Weakened by grief, they are unable to do what they wish.

verses.sanskrit: श्रमेण च विवर्णानां वक्त्राणां विप्लुतं वपुः। उत्तरं चाभिमन्युं च काम्भोजं च सुदक्षिणम्॥३४॥
verses.english: Scorched by the Sun, and exhausted with fatigue and toil, their faces have become colourless and pale.

verses.sanskrit: शिशीनेतान् हतान् पश्य लक्ष्मणं सुदर्शनम्। आयोधनशिरोमध्ये शयानं पश्य माधव॥३५॥
verses.english: See also, O Madhava, those other children besides Abhimanyu, viz., Uttara, Sudakshina the prince of the Kamvojas, and the beautiful Lakshmana, all lying on the field of battle.'
verses.bhavadeepa: वपुः शस्ताकृतिः ‘वपुः क्लीबं तनौ शस्ताकृतावपि’ इति मेदिनो॥३४॥
